```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

exploreDE reads one file format: an `.h5ad` (AnnData) file built by
`build_explore_h5ad()`. That function is the only supported way to get your
own data into the app, whatever pipeline produced it. This vignette covers:

1. installing exploreDE and running it on your own machine;
2. building a file, from counts only up to counts + DE + pathways;
3. checking the file before you open it;
4. what to do when your column names aren't recognised.

Every example below runs as written against the two datasets that ship with
the package (`inst/examples/`).

## Install and run

```{r install, eval = FALSE}
install.packages("BiocManager")
BiocManager::install("fgcz/exploreDE")   # pulls in the Bioconductor dependencies
```

Start the app with:

```{r run, eval = FALSE}
library(exploreDE)
exploreDE("my_data.h5ad")   # open straight into your file
exploreDE()                 # or start on the landing page
```

On the landing page, use **Choose an exploreDE .h5ad file** to upload
your file (up to 1 GB), or load the demo dataset. The file is read into memory for your session only.
The menu then shows only the tabs your data supports: DE tabs need a DE
table, pathway tabs need pathway results.

## What goes into a file

Only three things are required:

| Argument  | What it is |
|-----------|------------|
| `x`       | the counts: a matrix (features × samples), a named list of matrices (e.g. `list(counts = , normalised = )`), or a `DESeqDataSet` |
| `coldata` | sample metadata, one row per sample, rownames = the counts' column names |
| `omics`   | `"rnaseq"`, `"proteomics"` or `"crispr"` |

Everything else is optional: `rowdata` (feature annotation), `de` (one DE
table per contrast), `pathways` (ORA/GSEA results per contrast), plus labels
such as `organism`, `ref_build` and `factors`.

```{r libs, message = FALSE}
library(exploreDE)
library(SummarizedExperiment)
out_dir <- tempdir()
```

### Counts only

The shipped RNA-seq example is a SUSHI/DESeq2 result. Using only its counts
and sample table gives the smallest valid file:

```{r counts-only}
se <- readRDS(system.file("examples/genomics/deResult.rds", package = "exploreDE"))

build_explore_h5ad(
  assay(se, "counts"),
  out     = file.path(out_dir, "counts_only.h5ad"),
  omics   = "rnaseq",
  coldata = colData(se)
)
```

### Proteomics with one contrast

The shipped proteomics example is a prolfqua result. Its DE table sits in
`rowData` as a nested table, with prolfqua's own column names (`diff`,
`p.value`, `FDR`). You pass it as it is; the column dictionary (below)
recognises those names.

```{r proteomics}
se_prot <- readRDS(system.file("examples/proteomics/SummarizedExperiment.rds",
                               package = "exploreDE"))
de_prot <- as.data.frame(rowData(se_prot)$constrast_B_vs_A)

build_explore_h5ad(
  x       = list(raw = assay(se_prot, "rawData"),
                 transformed = assay(se_prot, "transformedData")),
  out     = file.path(out_dir, "proteomics.h5ad"),
  omics   = "proteomics",
  coldata = colData(se_prot),
  rowdata = de_prot,
  factors = "G_",
  de      = list(B_vs_A = de_prot)
)
```

### RNA-seq with DE and pathways

The same SUSHI result, this time with everything: two count layers, feature
annotation, the DE statistics (SUSHI keeps them in `rowData`) and the
clusterProfiler ORA and GSEA results from its metadata.

```{r rnaseq-full}
build_explore_h5ad(
  x         = list(counts = assay(se, "counts"), normalised = assay(se, "xNorm")),
  out       = file.path(out_dir, "rnaseq_full.h5ad"),
  omics     = "rnaseq",
  organism  = "Homo sapiens",
  ref_build = metadata(se)$param$refBuild,
  coldata   = colData(se),
  rowdata   = rowData(se),
  factors   = "Condition [Factor]",
  de        = list(diff_vs_undiff = rowData(se)),
  pathways  = list(diff_vs_undiff = list(ora  = metadata(se)$enrichResult,
                                          gsea = metadata(se)$enrichResultGSEA))
)
```

`de` and `pathways` are named by contrast; add one entry per contrast.

Pathway results can be clusterProfiler objects (`enrichResult`,
`gseaResult`), plain data.frames, or nested lists of either (as above:
BP/MF/CC × up/down/both). A plain data.frame must use clusterProfiler's
column names: `ID`, `Description`, `p.adjust`, `GeneRatio`, `Count`,
`geneID` for ORA, plus `enrichmentScore`, `NES`, `setSize`,
`core_enrichment` for GSEA. clusterProfiler objects are filtered to
`p.adjust <= enrichment_padj_max` (default 0.1); data.frames are stored as
given. With clusterProfiler objects, the network, ridge and running-score
plots are available too; with data.frames, the table-based pathway plots
are.

## Check the file before you open it

```{r check}
eds <- new_explore_dataset(file.path(out_dir, "rnaseq_full.h5ad"))
eds

eds$has_de()                                   # TRUE: a DE table was supplied
eds$has_pvalue()                               # TRUE only if a raw p-value was found
d <- eds$de(eds$primary_contrast())
c(log2fc_missing = all(is.na(d$effect_log2fc)),
  fdr_missing    = all(is.na(d$score_fdr)))   # both should be FALSE
```

If a DE column wasn't recognised it comes through as `NA` rather than as an
error, so do this check before trusting the file.

## How columns are recognised

You don't tell `build_explore_h5ad()` which column is the log2 fold change,
the p-value or the FDR. A dictionary shipped with the package
(`inst/dictionaries/column_patterns.json`) holds an ordered list of
case-insensitive patterns per concept. The first pattern that matches any
column wins, so exact names beat loose substrings:

```json
"effect_log2fc": ["^diff$", "^log2[._ ]?(fold)?[._ ]?(change|ratio|fc)?$",
                  "^logfc$", "^estimate$", "log2"],
"score_pvalue":  ["^p[._ ]?value$"],
"score_fdr":     ["^fdr$", "^adj[._ ]?p[._ ]?val(ue)?$", "^padj$",
                  "^q[._ ]?val(ue)?$", "^p[._ ]?adjusted$", "fdr"],
"score":         ["score"]
```

This covers DESeq2, edgeR, limma and prolfqua out of the box. It also
covers SAINTexpress, whose tables have `log2_EFCs`, `BFDR` and
`SaintScore` and no p-value at all: `log2_EFCs` matches `log2`, `BFDR`
matches `fdr`, and `SaintScore` becomes an extra score. That score is shown
in the DE table and offered as a volcano y-axis; significance thresholds
still use the FDR. With no p-value, the app works from the FDR alone.

The `rowdata` side works the same way for gene IDs, symbols, descriptions,
protein and peptide IDs, phospho sites and GO columns.

Only the recognised statistics are stored for each contrast. Other DE-table
columns (e.g. a per-contrast `avgAbd`) are not kept; put per-feature
annotation in `rowdata`, where every column is kept.

### When a column isn't recognised

`build_explore_h5ad()` warns, naming the contrast, the field it couldn't
fill and the columns it saw. Two fixes:

- **For one file:** name the columns yourself. Five keys exist; anything you
  don't name is still found by the dictionary.

  ```{r overrides, eval = FALSE}
  build_explore_h5ad(...,
    de_columns      = list(effect_log2fc = "<your column>",
                           score_pvalue  = "<your column>",
                           score_fdr     = "<your column>"),
    rowdata_columns = list(id_col = "<your column>", symbol_col = "<your column>"))
  ```

  `de_columns` applies to every contrast, or pass a list of such lists
  named by contrast. The mapping is saved in the file.

- **For a naming convention you'll see again:** add a pattern to
  `inst/dictionaries/column_patterns.json`. It's a JSON edit, not a code
  change; put anchored patterns (`^...$`) before loose ones.

### Feature level

`feature_level` is detected from `rowdata`: a `site` column means phospho, a
`peptide_Id` column means peptide, and a `transcript_id` column with one
transcript per row means isoform. Otherwise it's gene (RNA-seq) or protein
(proteomics). Pass `feature_level =` to override.
